question: If sin A = 0.6, what is the value of tan A ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given sin A = 0.6 = 6 ÷ 10 = 3 ÷ 5 = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), we directly get Base = 4.

tan A = Perpendicular ÷ Base

tan A = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75

**∴ The correct answer is 0.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A = 0.6

**Formula Used:**

sin² A + cos² A = 1

tan A = sin A ÷ cos A

 
 
 
 A A C B Base = 4 Perp = 3 Hyp = 5 

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos A = √(1 − sin² A)

⇒ cos A = √(1 − 0.6²)

⇒ cos A = √(1 − 0.36)

⇒ cos A = √0.64

⇒ cos A = 0.8

⇒ tan A = sin A ÷ cos A

⇒ tan A = 0.6 ÷ 0.8

⇒ tan A = 6 ÷ 8 = 3 ÷ 4

⇒ tan A = 0.75

**∴ The correct answer is 0.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle: sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse | tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three integers satisfying Pythagoras Theorem (a² + b² = c²). Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Their multiples like (6, 8, 10) are also valid triplets.

Fundamental Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ | 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.
